Quinn Iverson

Wellpoint Commercial/ACA Plan – New Jersey  

Date: [Date sent]

To: Wellpoint Appeals Department  
[Appeals mailing address or submission method]

Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Requested service: Total ankle replacement  
CPT: 27702  
Reference number: POC-E14E3A00BC-47205  
Date of denial notice: August 14, 2026  

Dear Wellpoint Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of coverage for the total ankle replacement requested by my orthopedic surgeon, Okafor, MD. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery.

The clinical record does document extensive conservative treatment, including:

- Progressive ankle pain for 18 months, unrelieved by rest.
- Four months of NSAID treatment, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 5, 2026, which provided only three weeks of partial relief.
- Sixteen weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance, from March 24, 2026, through July 14, 2026, with 20 visits completed. The physical therapy discharge note documents this treatment.
- Continued functional limitation despite these measures, including an antalgic gait and the ability to walk only approximately two blocks.
- Pain-limited range of motion and positive provocative testing on examination.

The objective findings also establish advanced ankle disease. Weight-bearing ankle radiographs obtained on July 17, 2026, show obliteration of the tibiotalar joint space with subchondral cysts. These findings, together with the persistent symptoms, failed conservative treatment, and substantial limitation in walking, support the medical necessity of total ankle replacement.

The records further show that there are no identified clinical barriers such as active infection, untreated substance use, or smoking. My BMI is 29. The requested surgery is being recommended after appropriate nonoperative care has been attempted and has not provided lasting or adequate relief.

The denial notice did not identify the specific medical policy, clinical guideline, version, or criteria used to determine that the documented treatment was inadequate. I am not quoting a Wellpoint policy because the applicable policy text was not provided with the denial and has not been verified. Please identify and provide the exact policy or clinical-review criteria applied to CPT 27702, including its effective date and the specific reason the documented 16-week physical therapy course, 20 completed visits, four months of NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection were considered insufficient.

Please conduct a complete reconsideration of this denial using the enclosed records. If any additional information is required, please notify me and my surgeon promptly. I request approval for the total ankle replacement and all medically necessary associated services.

Enclosures:

1. Adverse benefit determination dated August 14, 2026  
2. Physical therapy discharge note documenting treatment from March 24, 2026, through July 14, 2026, and 20 completed visits  
3. Medication and treatment history  
4. Corticosteroid injection record dated May 5, 2026  
5. Weight-bearing ankle radiographs and report dated July 17, 2026  
6. Orthopedic examination and surgical recommendation from Okafor, MD  
7. Other supporting clinical records

Please send the appeal determination and any requested policy materials to:

Quinn Iverson
